source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus spans two facilities with 40 MW of IT load published, making it the largest by capacity among five facilities with disclosed figures in North Carolina and accounting for 80 percent of the state's published data center power. At standard AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this 40 MW would support roughly 1,000 racks, though the operator's actual tenant mix and utilization are not published. The campus occupies 420,000 square feet across two codes, DUR1 and DUR2.

No certifications are listed for this campus in the operator's published specifications. The facility's regional standing and power commitment should be read against the broader North Carolina mapped inventory of 19 data centers, most of which do not publish power figures.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on what it is built to supply: its published IT capacity is substantial for a single operator site, but its current service to AI workloads, power supply agreements, and headroom for expansion are not disclosed. The state's total published capacity of 50 MW remains small relative to the grid build-out required if AI demand accelerates.
